verdicts.text: The Pulumi for Terraform Users guide covers referencing existing Terraform state files from Pulumi, using any Terraform provider in Pulumi programs, importing and using Terraform modules directly, converting HCL to Pulumi, and orchestrating Terraform and Pulumi deployments together.
verdicts.evidence: The guide's landing page lists all five topics: "Reference existing Terraform state files from Pulumi · Use any Terraform provider in Pulumi programs · Import and use Terraform modules directly · Convert HCL code to Pulumi when beneficial · Orchestrate both Terraform and Pulumi deployments together". There are also separate step pages for providers, modules, and orchestration. The claim drops the qualifier "when beneficial", which doesn't change the meaning.
verdicts.framing_note: The claim restates the guide's own five-item list of learning outcomes (landing page); it only drops "when beneficial" from the HCL-conversion item.

verdicts.text: 5. **Consider migration**: When ready, plan a gradual migration to Pulumi for new projects
verdicts.evidence: This line is advice from the author ("When ready, plan a gradual migration"). It isn't a falsifiable statement. The regex flagged it as temporal because of the phrase "When ready", which isn't a claim about dates or recency.

verdicts.text: `new pulumi.StackReference("core-infra")` with `getOutput("vpcId")` is valid for referencing outputs of another stack.
verdicts.evidence: The SDK defines `constructor(name: string, args?: StackReferenceArgs, opts?: CustomResourceOptions)`, and "If args is not specified, the name of the referenced stack will be the name of the StackReference resource". It also defines `public getOutput(name: Input<string>): Output<any>`, so `new pulumi.StackReference("core-infra").getOutput("vpcId")` is a valid call.
verdicts.intuition_flag: The API call is valid, but the example has two problems. A bare "core-infra" only finds a stack with that name in the current org and project; a separate project would need "org/project/stack". Also, the core stack in the snippet exports `vpc`, not `vpcId`, so `getOutput("vpcId")` would return undefined.

verdicts.text: The `terraform.state.S3Reference` resource (from `@pulumi/terraform`) exists and accepts `bucket` and `key` arguments to reference Terraform state stored in S3, with a `getOutput` method.
verdicts.evidence: The `@pulumi/terraform` Node.js SDK `state` module has no `S3Reference` class. It exports only the functions `getAzureRMReference`, `getLocalReference`, `getRemoteReference` and `getS3Reference` (each also has an `...Output` form): `export const getS3Reference: typeof import("./getS3Reference").getS3Reference`. `getS3Reference` is an invoke that returns the state outputs. Nothing in `state/index.ts` defines a `getOutput` method, so `new terraform.state.S3Reference(...)` and `.getOutput(...)` at L57/69/74/122/203/248 won't work as written.
verdicts.source: gh api repos/pulumi/pulumi-terraform/contents/sdk/nodejs/state/index.ts (and directory listing of sdk/nodejs/state)
verdicts.intuition_flag: This looks like an invented API modeled on the old `RemoteStateReference` class. The docs should use `terraform.state.getS3ReferenceOutput({bucket, key})` and read its outputs instead.

verdicts.text: ### Complex state referencing
verdicts.evidence: The text is just a markdown section heading ("### Complex state referencing"). It makes no factual assertion, and nothing is attributed to a third party. The regex flagged the capitalized word "Complex" as a source by mistake.

verdicts.text: The `aws.ecs.Cluster` resource accepts a `configuration.executeCommandConfiguration` argument with `kmsKeyId` and `logging` properties (with value "DEFAULT").
verdicts.evidence: The pulumi-aws Node.js SDK example for `aws.ecs.Cluster` uses `configuration: { executeCommandConfiguration: { ..., kmsKeyId: example.arn, logging: "OVERRIDE" } }`, so both `kmsKeyId` and `logging` exist on `configuration.executeCommandConfiguration`. `logging` is a string field. "DEFAULT" is a valid ECS value (NONE, DEFAULT or OVERRIDE), though the file I fetched only shows OVERRIDE.
verdicts.framing_note: The fetched source shows the property shape. The "DEFAULT" value comes from ECS's documented logging enum, which I did not fetch this session.

verdicts.text: `pulumi import` can be used to bring Terraform-managed resources under Pulumi management.
verdicts.evidence: The auto-generated CLI reference says "Resources that are not managed by Pulumi can be imported into a Pulumi stack using this command." It also lists `--from string  Invoke a converter to import the resources`, which is how Terraform-managed resources get imported (for example `--from terraform`).
verdicts.framing_note: The source covers any resources not managed by Pulumi. Terraform-managed resources are one case of that.

verdicts.text: State ownership can be transferred gradually, resource-by-resource, from Terraform to Pulumi.
verdicts.evidence: Pulumi's migration guide says you can import resources "in the usual way" (`pulumi import`, one resource at a time) or adopt everything from a .tfstate with `pulumi import --from terraform`. That makes a gradual, resource-by-resource handoff possible. A third-party guide adds that you should run `terraform state rm` after each import so the two tools don't both try to own the same resource.
verdicts.framing_note: This is a general capability claim. It is backed by per-resource `pulumi import`. The Terraform side still has to be released by hand with `terraform state rm`, so "transferred" is really a two-step process.
verdicts.intuition_flag: The claim leaves out that Terraform needs `terraform state rm` to give up each resource. Without that step, both tools end up owning the same resource. The encore.dev guide also warns against splitting ownership per resource inside a single module.

verdicts.text: `pulumi import` accepts the syntax `pulumi import <type> <name> <id>` with types like `aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc`, `aws:ec2/subnet:Subnet`, `aws:ecs/cluster:Cluster`.
verdicts.evidence: The auto-generated CLI reference says "If using the command line args directly, the type token, name, id and optional flags must be provided. For example: pulumi import 'aws:iam/user:User' name id". It also uses "aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc" as an example type. aws:ec2/subnet:Subnet and aws:ecs/cluster:Cluster follow the same standard AWS provider token format, but I did not check those two separately.

verdicts.text: Pulumi policies (CrossGuard) can enforce infrastructure policies across both Terraform and Pulumi.
verdicts.evidence: The Pulumi Policies docs say policies apply to Terraform-provisioned resources only in audit mode: "Audit: Continuously scans resources discovered through Insights Discovery to identify violations across all infrastructure, including resources created with Terraform... Provides visibility without blocking operations." Blocking enforcement is described only for Pulumi stacks during `pulumi preview`/`up`, and audit mode needs Pulumi Cloud. So "enforce across both" overstates what policies do for Terraform, and the example policy pack only runs against Pulumi stacks.
verdicts.framing_note: Docs support preventative enforcement for Pulumi stacks plus audit-only (non-blocking) scans of Terraform resources through Insights Discovery. The claim describes this as enforcement across both.

verdicts.text: `@pulumi/policy` exports `PolicyPack` and `validateResourceOfType`, and policies accept `name`, `description`, `enforcementLevel: "mandatory"`, and `validateResource` with signature (resource, args, reportViolation).
verdicts.evidence: The pulumi-policy SDK exports `PolicyPack` and `validateResourceOfType`. `Policy` has `name`, `description`, and `enforcementLevel?: EnforcementLevel` (which includes "mandatory"), and `ResourceValidationPolicy` has `validateResource`. The SDK's own doc example matches the page's code line for line: `validateResource: validateResourceOfType(aws.s3.Bucket, (bucket, args, reportViolation) => {`.
verdicts.framing_note: The three-parameter signature (resource, args, reportViolation) belongs to the callback passed to validateResourceOfType. A bare `validateResource` callback takes (args, reportViolation). The page's code is correct; only the claim's wording is loose.

verdicts.text: `aws.s3.Bucket` has an `acl` property with values such as "public-read" and "public-read-write".
verdicts.evidence: The pulumi-aws SDK source for `aws.s3.Bucket` has an `acl` property: "Valid values are `private`, `public-read`, `public-read-write`, `aws-exec-read`, `authenticated-read`, and `log-delivery-write`." The property is marked "@deprecated acl is deprecated. Use the aws.s3.BucketAcl resource instead."
verdicts.framing_note: The property still exists, but it is deprecated in favor of aws.s3.BucketAcl. The docs may want to mention that.

verdicts.text: The Pulumi Automation API allows embedding Pulumi in applications for dynamic infrastructure management.
verdicts.evidence: The Automation API README in pulumi/pulumi calls it "the programmatic interface for driving Pulumi programs without the CLI." Its listed uses include "Using pulumi behind a REST or GRPC API" and "Building higher level tools, custom CLIs over pulumi". That backs the claim that it lets you embed Pulumi in applications to manage infrastructure dynamically.

verdicts.text: Automation API provides `LocalWorkspace.createOrSelectStack` with `stackName`, `projectName`, and `program` options, `stack.setConfig`, and `stack.up({ onOutput })` returning `outputs`.
verdicts.evidence: In sdk/nodejs/automation/stack.ts, `async up(opts?: UpOptions): Promise<UpResult>` passes `opts?.onOutput` to runPulumiCmd and then runs `const outputs = await this.outputs()` to build the result. The Stack class supports createOrSelect. `LocalWorkspace.createOrSelectStack` taking InlineProgramArgs {stackName, projectName, program}, and `Stack.setConfig`, are standard parts of the same SDK, but I didn't read them directly because localWorkspace.ts returned an error.

verdicts.text: `terraform.state.S3Reference` is accessible as `pulumi.terraform.state.S3Reference` from the `@pulumi/pulumi/automation` import.
verdicts.evidence: sdk/nodejs/automation/index.ts (base64-decoded) contains only `export * from "./cmd"; "./config"; "./errors"; "./stack"; "./stackSettings"; "./projectSettings"; "./localWorkspace"; "./workspace"; "./events"; "./remoteStack"; "./remoteWorkspace"; "./tag";`. It has no `terraform` namespace, so `pulumi.terraform.state.S3Reference` does not exist on the `@pulumi/pulumi/automation` import. Terraform state references come from the separate `@pulumi/terraform` package, which is how the same page imports it at L245.
verdicts.intuition_flag: `S3Reference` may not exist in @pulumi/terraform either (that package exposes `state.RemoteStateReference`); I couldn't confirm because GitHub code search hit its rate limit.

verdicts.text: Component resources can integrate with Terraform behind the scenes, hiding multi-tool complexity from development teams and leaving it to the platform team.
verdicts.evidence: The components concept page says components let "consumers create complex infrastructure through a simple, well-defined interface—without needing to know the implementation details." So a component can read Terraform state (as the page's WebApplication example does with `getOutput` on a Terraform state reference) while hiding that complexity from the teams that use it. The "platform team vs development teams" split is advice, not a product fact.
verdicts.intuition_flag: The code sample on L248 uses `terraform.state.S3Reference`. The class I'd expect in @pulumi/terraform is `RemoteStateReference`, so `S3Reference` may not exist. I couldn't confirm this because GitHub search was rate-limited.

verdicts.text: `pulumi.ComponentResource` constructor is `super(type, name, args, opts)` with `pulumi.ComponentResourceOptions`, and `registerOutputs` is available.
verdicts.evidence: I fetched sdk/nodejs/resource.ts from pulumi/pulumi, but the output was cut off before the ComponentResource class, and code search hit a rate limit, so I couldn't quote the lines. From what I know of the @pulumi/pulumi SDK, the constructor is `constructor(type: string, name: string, args: Inputs = {}, opts: ComponentResourceOptions = {}, remote?, packageRef?)` and there is a protected `registerOutputs(outputs?)` method. That makes `super(type, name, args, opts)` together with `registerOutputs` accurate, but I did not confirm it this session.
verdicts.source: gh api repos/pulumi/pulumi/contents/sdk/nodejs/resource.ts (output truncated before ComponentResource class)
verdicts.framing_note: The constructor also takes optional trailing parameters (`remote`, `packageRef`). The claim leaves them out, but it doesn't say anything that conflicts with them.
